cultural.vision_reason: This is a Thai Buddhist votive amulet depicting Khun Chang, a figure from a Thai folk epic, worn as a personal amulet in presentation packaging — a traditional Thai ritual/devotional object rather than jewelry per se.

physical.title: tablet; amulet
physical.summary: Votive tablet of Khun Chang. Votive sealing or amulet bearing a high-relief depiction of Khun Chang, the anti-hero of Khun Chang Khun Phaen, a popular traditional Thai story. The plump bare-chested figure squats with his right leg curled in front of him and the left upright and bent. The right hand grips his money bag. On the back of the sealing is a magic symbol. The sealing has a rectangular shape with a rounded top and is made of an impressed white substance. It is in a small standard-style presentation box for amulets, plastic with a hinged cover with machine-inscribed floral and other motifs and the name of the figure and the monastery in Thai, and a red velvet-like cushion.

cultural.vision_reason: A printed cloth amulet depicting the Phra Chinarat Buddha (a famous Thai Buddha image) with Thai and Chinese text and yantra diagrams, worn/used as a protective ritual object in Thai Buddhist practice — this is a ritual amulet, not jewelry in the ornamental sense.

physical.title: amulet; yantra
physical.summary: Yellow printed cloth amulet. Cloth amulet printed with an image of the Phra Chinarat Buddha statue flanked by two female bodhisattvas (enlightened beings) wearing Chinese dress and with halos around their heads. The Buddha image is seated and framed within a decorated frame. Below him is Thai text including the name of the image and a recitation for honoring it. At the top, sides and bottom are the name of the image and monastery and wishes for well-being in Chinese. In the lower section are magic diagrams. The whole is bordered by a flower motif.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a Thai Buddhist amulet plaque depicting Maitreya, with Khom and Thai script naming a Thai monastery (Wat Lai) — a devotional object made and worn by Thai people, fitting the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: amulet
physical.summary: Large, gold-coloured plaque with Buddha image. Amuletic plate of metal stamped with a seated image of Maitreya Buddha on a lotus throne. His right hand is extended over his leg, and his left hand makes a gesture with the pointer and little fingers extended. At the top of the plaque are letters in Khom script, and at the bottom, an epithet of Maitreya in Thai and the name and location of the monastery, Wat Lai, also in Thai.
